verdict.lesson_authoring: Do not begin polished prose, figure code, SVG drawing, or demo implementation until the metric and dataset blockers in this report are resolved.
verdict.reason: The course spine, prerequisite DFT lesson, preceding DTMF close, concept registry, research brief, and canonical Harris audit all agree on one lesson move: finite observation creates a window kernel whose main lobe, sidelobes, coherent gain, scalloping, and ENBW must be measured as a coupled choice. The remaining uncertainty is not conceptual or evidentiary; it is the exact numerical and convention contract from which future prose, plots, and the phase-robust demo must be generated.

course_contract.spine_claim: Finite records trade leakage against resolution, and isolated-tone interpolation cannot manufacture observation time.
course_contract.spine_caption: Window metrics replace visual preference with measurement.
course_contract.goal: Evaluate analysis windows from main-lobe width, sidelobes, coherent gain, scalloping, and equivalent noise bandwidth.
course_contract.required_opening_verbatim: Finite observation convolves the desired spectrum with the window transform, so every leakage repair changes resolution and calibration.
key_ideas: Leakage is caused by finite observation, not sampling.
Narrow main lobes and low sidelobes conflict.
Coherent gain and ENBW calibrate signal and noise.

demo.required_contract: Detect a -40 dB tone 5.5 original bins from a stronger tone by choosing window and record length before relative phase is randomized. Pass only when the weak peak remains at least 3 dB above local leakage for every tested phase; rectangular-window failure falsifies narrowest-is-best.

next_lesson.title: Peak Estimation and Zero-Padding Limits
next_lesson.opening: A sampled main lobe can locate one isolated tone between bins, but denser FFT samples do not add observation time or separate unresolved components.
next_lesson.boundary: The target lesson owns window choice and calibration. The next lesson owns window-dependent isolated-tone interpolation, zero-padding as denser sampling of the same DTFT, and the distinction between coordinate accuracy and physical resolution.

concept_contract.analysis_window_exact_definition: A finite weighting w[n] applied to a record or frame before spectral analysis.
concept_contract.spectral_leakage_exact_definition: Spreading caused when finite observation convolves a signal spectrum with the window transform.
concept_contract.reinforced_dft_exact_definition: The N orthogonal complex frequency coefficients of an N-sample record under an explicit normalization.
concept_contract.next_spectral_resolution_exact_definitio: The ability of a finite observation and window to support distinct frequency claims, not merely the spacing of plotted FFT samples.
concept_contract.scope_rule: Use the first two definitions explicitly. Reinforce the DFT convention without re-teaching inversion, real symmetry, or FFT factorization. Do not define spectral resolution as a new concept here; prepare its measurement boundary and leave the formal concept to the next lesson.

inherits: Raw negative-sign forward DFT and 1/N inverse convention.
Half-open sample index 0 <= n < N and explicit natural/signed frequency coordinates.
The identity that DFT coefficients sample the finite-record DTFT at omega_k=2*pi*k/N.
The distinction between N acquired samples and a longer transform length L used only to sample the same finite-record DTFT more densely.
The fact that an off-bin finite cosine produces nonzero values across DFT coordinates.
must_not_repeat: Full DFT derivation or roots-of-unity proof.
formal_prerequisite.exact_retrieval_ref: <Ref lesson="dft-bins-symmetry-and-scaling">DFT Bins, Symmetry, and Scaling</Ref> established that an N-point DFT samples the continuous transform of one finite record and that padding changes the plotted coordinates without changing the observed samples.

immediate_predecessor.exact_closing_handoff: The receiver contract is now auditable: spectral coordinates, named-profile gates, temporal state, latency origins, and arithmetic units are separated, and the held-out study preserves both passed and failed targets. Windows, Leakage, and Resolution next measures how the rectangular record's main lobe and sidelobes hide the weak neighboring line and how a changed window trades that leakage against resolution and calibration.
immediate_predecessor.exact_forward_exercise_handoff: A reproducible comparison freezes the sampling rate, physical tone frequencies, amplitudes, relative-phase cases, noise rule, estimator coordinates, and amplitude calibration. It varies padding length, acquired duration, and window family separately. For each run it reports grid spacing, observation time, main-lobe width, peak sidelobe level, coherent gain, scalloping loss, equivalent noise bandwidth, and whether the weak line remains stable under relative-phase changes. Those measurements separate display density from physical evidence and make the window choice a declared tradeoff. <Ref lesson="windows-leakage-and-resolution">Windows, Leakage, and Resolution</Ref> derives the window metrics needed to execute that comparison.

frozen_failure_to_reuse.inference: Zero padding samples the same response more densely and cannot remove this masking.

immediate_predecessor.target_opening_bridge: <Ref lesson="phone-channel-dtmf-receiver">Phone-Channel DTMF Receiver</Ref> left one controlled failure unresolved: a half-bin strong line under a rectangular record sits 26.5359 dB above a -40 dB neighbor at the neighbor's coordinate, and padding does not change that kernel.

continuity.continuity_distinction: The lesson must not imply that the DTMF application is a formal prerequisite. The DFT lesson supplies the mathematical contract; the immediately preceding DTMF lesson supplies the concrete engineering failure. Both belong in the opening throughline, with their different roles stated.

forward_handoff.exact_proposed_closing: Window choice is now measurable: the record kernel's main lobe and sidelobes set deterministic interference, while coherent gain, scalloping, and ENBW calibrate tone and noise claims. What remains unresolved is how to locate one isolated tone between displayed coordinates without mistaking a denser grid for longer observation. <Ref lesson="peak-estimation-and-zero-padding">Peak Estimation and Zero-Padding Limits</Ref> next separates window-dependent interpolation from physical resolution.
forward_handoff.exercise_rule: Exactly one closing exercise should reach forward. It must hold acquired samples and window fixed, vary only transform length, name the changed interpolation grid and unchanged window transform, and include one Ref to peak-estimation-and-zero-padding in its solution.

Defining or calibrating coherent gain, scalloping, or ENBW.
Explaining the rectangular-window DTMF masking failure.

proposed_opening_throughline.sentence_1_verbatim: Finite observation convolves the desired spectrum with the window transform, so every leakage repair changes resolution and calibration.
proposed_opening_throughline.paragraph_1_after_sentence_1: Use the DTMF failure as the concrete problem: a narrow rectangular main lobe did not protect a -40 dB neighbor from the strong line's sidelobe, and padding could only reveal the same masking curve more densely.
proposed_opening_throughline.paragraph_2: Retrieve the prerequisite result that a DFT samples one finite-record DTFT. Name multiplication by w[n] and frequency-domain convolution only after the learner has seen the periodic boundary mismatch and its tapered repair.
proposed_opening_throughline.paragraph_3: State the lesson's single move: replace visual window preference with five declared measurements, then test the choice against one phase-robust weak-tone claim.
proposed_opening_throughline.route_sentence: The route is finite-observation leakage, endpoint behavior and lobe shape, deterministic-tone calibration, noise calibration, and a controlled weak-neighbor decision.

retrieval_gate.placement: After the opening throughline and before new definitions.
retrieval_gate.mode: One compact Task with a folded answer; space the same knowledge later rather than repeating it immediately.

prompts.prompt: For N acquired samples, state the frequencies sampled by the N-point DFT and what changes if the same record is padded to transform length L>N.
prompts.success: omega_k=2*pi*k/N for the original DFT; padding changes evaluation spacing to 2*pi/L but not the acquired duration or finite-record DTFT.

prompts.prompt: Write the course raw forward DFT sign and scale convention.
prompts.success: X[k]=sum from n=0 to N-1 of x[n] exp(-j2*pi*k*n/N), with no forward normalization.

prompts.prompt: Classify changing sample rate, padding length, acquired duration, and window as possible repairs for aliasing, denser plotting, narrower finite-record response, and lower sidelobes.
prompts.success: Sample-rate/front-end changes address aliasing; padding only densifies coordinates; longer acquisition changes response width; a window changes main lobe, sidelobes, and calibration together.

prompts.prompt: Why can a single off-bin sinusoid produce many nonzero DFT coordinates without implying many physical tones?
prompts.success: The finite observation creates a continuous window-shaped spectrum that the DFT samples; nonzero coordinates are leakage from the finite record, not a list of separate sources.

retrieval_gate.pass_rule: Proceed when R1 and R4 are correct and at least one of R2 or R3 is correct. Route R1/R2 misses to the DFT lesson and R3/R4 misses to the predecessor's final leakage exercise.

argument_skeleton.heading: Finite observation creates leakage before an FFT is chosen
argument_skeleton.running_question: Why does one off-bin tone spread when the sampled signal itself contains no extra tones?
argument_skeleton.seam_from_prior: The DFT grid describes where the finite-record transform is sampled; it does not explain the transform's shape between those coordinates.
argument_skeleton.concrete_entry: Periodically extend an off-bin sinusoid over adjacent copies of the same half-open record, expose the boundary jump, then apply a taper and show the repaired join.
argument_skeleton.claim: Multiplying a record by w[n] convolves the desired spectrum with W(e^{j omega}); leakage is a finite-observation/window effect rather than sampling aliasing.
formal_apparatus: Define x_w[n]=x[n]w[n] for 0<=n<N.
Define W(e^{j omega}) with the course negative exponent.
State the 2*pi-periodic convolution formula with its 1/(2*pi) factor.
Introduce the exact concept definitions for analysis window and spectral leakage.
argument_skeleton.expectation_reversal: A smooth-looking zero-padded plot cannot repair the periodic boundary or change W; it only samples the already-windowed curve more densely.
argument_skeleton.seam_to_next: A taper can reduce the boundary jump, but the repair has a frequency-domain cost that must be measured.

argument_skeleton.heading: Endpoint smoothness lowers far sidelobes by widening the central lobe
argument_skeleton.running_question: Which visible property of w[n] predicts where leakage goes?
argument_skeleton.seam_from_prior: The convolution model says every tone inherits W; window selection therefore becomes selection of a spectral kernel.
argument_skeleton.concrete_entry: Compare rectangular, periodic Hann, Hamming, and one declared four-term Blackman-Harris window under identical N, centering, zero-padding-for-display, dB floor, and peak normalization.
argument_skeleton.claim: Smoother endpoint matching accelerates far-sidelobe decay, but concentration cannot be improved everywhere: lower sidelobes generally accompany a wider main lobe.
formal_apparatus: Declare periodic versus symmetric coefficient convention before naming a window.
Measure null-to-null main-lobe width and peak sidelobe level relative to W(0).
Distinguish peak sidelobe from asymptotic falloff.
Use Hann, not Hanning, and distinguish it from Hamming by endpoints and falloff.
argument_skeleton.expectation_reversal: The rectangular window's narrowest main lobe does not make it best when a strong neighbor sets the leakage floor.
argument_skeleton.seam_to_next: Lobe shape controls interference, but even a perfectly isolated bin-centered tone is attenuated by the window and therefore needs calibration.

argument_skeleton.heading: Coherent gain and scalloping calibrate deterministic tones
argument_skeleton.running_question: How can equal physical tones produce different reported amplitudes under different windows and bin placements?
argument_skeleton.seam_from_prior: A kernel comparison normalized to W(0) hides the absolute attenuation applied to the measured tone.
argument_skeleton.concrete_entry: For periodic four-sample Hann w=[0,0.5,1,0.5], compute G_c=0.5, show the raw bin-centered complex-tone response sum(w)=2, and recover unit amplitude by dividing by N G_c; then move the tone half a bin to expose scalloping.
argument_skeleton.claim: Coherent gain removes window-dependent bin-centered amplitude bias, while scalloping loss quantifies the remaining worst placement loss between sampled coordinates.
formal_apparatus: Define normalized coherent gain G_c=(1/N)sum w[n].
Also name the unnormalized coherent response C_w=sum w[n]=N G_c so the brief's two phrasings cannot be confused.
Define scalloping as a positive loss in dB from W(0) to W(pi/N), with the sign convention displayed.
Separate complex-exponential and one-sided real-cosine amplitude factors.
argument_skeleton.expectation_reversal: No visible leakage is required for a wrong amplitude report; an uncorrected bin-centered tone is already biased by the taper.
argument_skeleton.seam_to_next: Signal amplitude uses the coherent sum of weights; broadband noise accumulates the squared weights and needs a different calibration.

argument_skeleton.heading: Equivalent noise bandwidth calibrates noise, not tone amplitude
argument_skeleton.running_question: Why does dividing by coherent gain not make noise floors comparable across windows?
argument_skeleton.seam_from_prior: A deterministic tone adds coherently through sum w[n], whereas independent white-noise samples add in power through sum w[n]^2.
argument_skeleton.concrete_entry: Reuse the four-sample periodic Hann: sum w=2, sum w^2=1.5, so B_e=4(1.5)/4=1.5 bins; compare with the rectangular window's one-bin ENBW.
argument_skeleton.claim: ENBW is the equal-peak-gain rectangular bandwidth that passes the same white-noise power; in bins B_e=N sum w[n]^2/(sum w[n])^2, and in hertz it is B_e f_s/N.
formal_apparatus: Derive ENBW from coherent signal gain and incoherent noise-power gain.
Keep bins, hertz, and radians/sample as explicitly converted units.
Do not introduce overlap correlation, hop R, or frame index ell here; those belong to Welch/STFT lessons.
argument_skeleton.expectation_reversal: Two spectra corrected to the same tone amplitude can still show different noise floors because their equivalent noise bandwidths differ.
argument_skeleton.visual: V3 WindowCalibrationLedger continues as a paired signal/noise comparison; no second decorative formula graphic
argument_skeleton.seam_to_next: The five metrics now predict costs, but a window is chosen only by a declared signal claim under a controlled dataset.

argument_skeleton.heading: A window is selected by the claim it must support
argument_skeleton.running_question: Which window and record length make a -40 dB neighbor defensible under phase changes?
argument_skeleton.seam_from_prior: Main-lobe width, sidelobes, coherent gain, scalloping, and ENBW are not a ranking until the detection task fixes what failure means.
argument_skeleton.concrete_entry: Return to the predecessor/Harris experiment: strong amplitude 1, weak amplitude 0.01, 5.5 original-bin separation, strong tone shifted off-grid, phase randomized only after window and N are chosen.
argument_skeleton.claim: No window is universally best. A choice passes this lesson's task only if the weak peak remains at least 3 dB above local leakage for every declared phase while its main-lobe width, signal calibration, and noise bandwidth remain reported.
formal_apparatus: Prediction Task before the demo asks which metric will limit rectangular, Hann, and four-term Blackman-Harris choices.
V4 makes the masking mechanism visible with fixed axes.
WeakToneWindowLab changes window and acquired N under one frozen signal/phase protocol.
V5 shows why worst-case loss versus peak sidelobe is informative but cannot crown a winner because coherent multitone behavior is omitted.

Close with a compact decision table: isolated tone in white noise emphasizes scalloping/ENBW; equal close tones emphasize main-lobe width; unequal close tones emphasize sidelobes plus main-lobe encroachment.
argument_skeleton.expectation_reversal: A window can look superior on a two-number tradeoff chart and still lose on coherent unequal-tone behavior; a scalar chart is evidence, not a universal ordering.
argument_skeleton.visual: V4 WeakToneMasking, WeakToneWindowLab, and V5 WindowTradeoffMap
argument_skeleton.seam_to_next: After the window and observation are fixed, a denser grid may improve one isolated peak estimate but cannot add resolving evidence.

keeper_fact_clusters: Padding changes coordinates, not the finite-observation kernel.

lesson_definitions.definition: sum from n=0 to N-1 of w[n] exp(-j omega n)
(1/(2*pi)) integral from -pi to pi of X(e^{j theta}) W(e^{j(omega-theta)}) d theta
sum from n=0 to N-1 of x[n]w[n] exp(-j2*pi*k*n/L)

lesson_definitions.name: positive scalloping loss
lesson_definitions.note: Use W(1) as shorthand for W(e^{j0}) only if the prose makes the zero-frequency evaluation explicit; otherwise write W(e^{j0}).

amplitude_contract.real_cosine_interior_bin_one_sided_peak_: A_hat=2|X_{w,N}[k_0]|/(N G_c), with the inherited DC/Nyquist singleton exception.
amplitude_contract.warning: The brief alternates between calling sum w[n] coherent gain and defining coherent gain as (sum w[n])/N. Freeze G_c as the normalized mean and C_w as the unnormalized response; display both once.

window_coefficients_to_freeze.hamming: Declare the exact coefficient pair and endpoint convention; do not mix 25/46 cancellation with rounded 0.54/0.46 claims.
window_coefficients_to_freeze.four_term_blackman_harris: Name and freeze one coefficient vector. Do not use 'four-term Blackman-Harris' as though the family had one unique member.

metric_definitions_to_freeze.main_lobe_width: Use null-to-null width in original N-point bins for the core comparison. If 3 dB or 6 dB width appears, label it separately and do not call all three 'resolution'.
metric_definitions_to_freeze.peak_sidelobe: Maximum sidelobe magnitude relative to |W(e^{j0})|, reported as a negative dB level.
metric_definitions_to_freeze.far_sidelobe_falloff: Asymptotic envelope slope in dB/octave; do not substitute it for peak sidelobe level.
metric_definitions_to_freeze.scalloping: Positive dB loss at the worst half-bin placement for the declared periodic window and N.
metric_definitions_to_freeze.worst_case_processing_loss: Do not plot until the adopted formula and sign are recorded in the derived-data artifact; Harris combines window processing loss with maximum scalloping loss.

symbols_intentionally_deferred.reason: Hop size is unused in this lesson's single-record goal and belongs to Welch/STFT.
Frame index is unused in the WeakToneWindowLab and belongs to later frame-based lessons.

exercise_architecture.only_mechanical: Periodic four-sample Hann: compute G_c, C_w, B_e, and calibrated bin-centered amplitude.
exercise_architecture.boundary_probe: Compare bin-centered, half-bin, equal-frequency, and two equal tones crossing at the separately declared 6 dB width; distinguish a degenerate equal-frequency sum from two resolved components.
exercise_architecture.claim_to_refute: Hann and Hamming differ only in spelling; refute using exact endpoint convention, first sidelobe, and far-sidelobe decay.
exercise_architecture.derivation_not_shown: Derive coherent/incoherent gain and ENBW for a short unseen window, then predict its relative noise floor after tone-amplitude correction.
exercise_architecture.strategy_choice: Choose rectangular versus the frozen four-term Blackman-Harris for equal close tones and for a -40 dB neighbor 5.5 bins away; state which measured result could overturn each choice.
exercise_architecture.forward: Hold samples and window fixed, increase only L, estimate one off-bin peak, and explain why interpolation changes while W and physical resolving evidence do not. The solution contains the sole forward exercise Ref.
exercise_architecture.anti_redundancy: Exercises must reuse the contract but not merely re-read values from V2/V3. At least two use unseen coefficient vectors or placements.

harris.coverage: Complete 33-page article; sections II-VII, Table I, Figure 12, and section VI unequal-tone experiment are locally audited.
harris.rights_note: The source audit records the paper as U.S. Government work not protected by U.S. copyright and openly served by CMU. This lesson still plans original analytic redraws rather than source-page crops.

other_sources.j_o_smith: Research read covers generalized Hamming, Blackman-Harris, endpoint/falloff comparisons, and measured oboe examples; use analytic claims here and reserve oboe artifacts for their assigned application lesson.
other_sources.mit_6341: Research read covers finite-record convolution, Kaiser tradeoffs, picket-fence sampling, zero padding, and resolvability; use only the window/finite-record portions owned by this lesson.
other_sources.oppenheim_schafer: Brief designates chapter 10 sections 10.1-10.4 as the finite-data/window reference.

authoring_guardrails: The opening sentence must be exact, including punctuation.
State that DTMF is the immediately preceding application but not the declared prerequisite.
Never say leakage is caused by sampling or repaired by changing sample rate alone.
Never call FFT-bin spacing physical resolution in this lesson.
Never present rectangular, Hann, Hamming, or Blackman-Harris as universally best.
Never compare raw peak amplitudes across windows without coherent-gain calibration.
Never compare noise floors without ENBW and unit declarations.
Never use 'Hann' and 'Hamming' interchangeably or use 'Hanning' as the formal name.
Never leave periodic versus symmetric endpoints implicit.
Never call a four-term Blackman-Harris family member unique without its coefficients.
Never let zero-padding change the claimed original-bin separation or acquired duration.
Never copy, crop, trace, or recolor Harris figures; generate original analytic visuals from checked data.
Never hand-draw fake roughness or sketch artifacts into raw SVGs.
Use components for formula-rich or label-dense comparison visuals and raw SVG for the four simple sequence frames plus the key image.
Use exactly one forward closing exercise with a Ref to peak-estimation-and-zero-padding.
